title: Two near-simultaneous weigh-in submits from different components both write, producing duplicate same-day body_weight_entries rows
steps: Open WeighInPrompt's 'Log weight' field on one tab (weight=182) and Progress > Weight tab's field on a second tab/session (weight=181, notes tagged). Fire both submit clicks with no await between them.
expected: Only one same-day body_weight_entries row exists (an upsert-by-date, per the code's own client-side select-then-branch intent), or the second write is rejected/merged.
actual: 2 rows created for today: {weight:181, notes:"OVN-body-r1-01"} and {weight:182, notes:null}. useLogWeight's select-then-create/update has no unique constraint or transactional guard, so two concurrent callers both read zero existing rows and both insert.
evidence: script console output; rowsForToday=2 before cleanup
suspectFile: src/hooks/useWeighIn.js (useLogWeight — client-side select-then-create/update, no DB unique constraint on created_by+recorded_date)
why: Code confirms useLogWeight (src/hooks/useWeighIn.js:100-122) is select-then-insert with no DB unique index on (created_by, recorded_date) (only a btree idx_body_weight_user_date), so two truly concurrent callers can both insert. But the repro needs two separate tabs/components submitting in the same instant. On the phone there is one screen: WeighInPrompt and the Progress Weight tab are never mounted together, and each button is disabled while its mutation is pending (WeighInPrompt.jsx:203, Progress.jsx:104), so a double tap on either one can't produce a second insert. Tested: new verify script scripts/r1-01v.mjs double-taps Progress > Log ~100ms apart on one screen and gets rows=1 (cleaned up). Not reachable by the real user. Optional hardening (needs a hosted migration plus dedup of existing rows, so Nolan's call): a unique index on (created_by, recorded_date) with the hook switched to upsert.

title: Weight tab (Progress) has no bounds check — an implausible value (1810 lbs) saves silently
steps: Open Progress > Weight tab, backdate 3 days, enter weight=1810, tap Log.
expected: A sanity bound (WeighInPrompt already has one: lbs 50-700 / kg 25-320) rejects or warns on an implausible value.
actual: Row saved with weight=1810, no warning or confirm shown, success toast displayed as if normal.
evidence: script console output: saved=true sawSuccessToast=true sawConfirmOrWarning=false
suspectFile: src/pages/Progress.jsx (Weight tab input has no min/max, unlike WeighInPrompt.jsx's existing bounds guard)
why: Re-ran r1-02: weight=1810 backdated 3 days saved with a success toast and no warning (row 3c941cfa, deleted in cleanup). Progress.jsx:42-56 hands the raw input to useLogWeight with no bounds, while WeighInPrompt.jsx:14 already has BOUNDS lbs 50-700 / kg 25-320. This is the same fat-finger class as train-logger-r1-01 (1710 for 171, confirmed). An entry for today would also overwrite profile.current_weight (useWeighIn.js:125), which drives the water goal and TDEE, and any date feeds the engine's weight trend.
fixHint: src/pages/Progress.jsx:42-47 - before mutateAsync, reuse WeighInPrompt's BOUNDS (export it from src/components/dashboard/WeighInPrompt.jsx:14) against profile.weight_unit and throw/toast.error('That weight looks off, check the number') when out of range, as WeighInPrompt does.

title: Measurements tab inserts a new row per save instead of upserting by date, and 'Latest' isn't deterministic
steps: Open Measurements tab, enter Chest=100 tagged '-am', save. Immediately enter Chest=101 tagged '-pm' for the same date, save again.
expected: Either the second save updates the same-date entry, or the 'Latest' card deterministically reflects the most recently saved value.
actual: 2 rows exist for the same date (chest 100 and 101). The 'Latest' card did not reliably show the most recent (101/pm) value — history query orders by date only, no created_at tiebreak.
suspectFile: src/pages/Progress.jsx:209-222 (insert, no upsert), :202 (order by date only, no secondary sort)
why: Re-ran r1-03: two rows for 2026-09-28 (chest 100 and 101), and the Latest card did not show the later 101 save. Progress.jsx:212-213 always inserts, and the history query (:202) orders by date only, so same-date rows come back in arbitrary order and history[0] 'Latest' (:233) can be the stale one. The realistic trigger is fixing a typo by re-saving: the fix may not show, and the TrendBadge then compares the same day's two values. Downgraded to minor: measurements only feed this card and DataExport (not the engine), and delete-with-confirm exists. Whether same-date saves should merge into one row is a design call; the ordering fix is not.
fixHint: src/pages/Progress.jsx:202 - add .order('created_at', { ascending: false }) after the date order so the newest same-day save is 'Latest'.

title: Typing dose '0' when logging a supplement silently falls back to the default dose instead of logging 0
steps: Type '0' into the dose field for a supplement type with default_dose=5. Tap Log.
expected: The logged dose is 0 (explicitly typed) or the UI explains why 0 is rejected.
actual: Logged row has dose=5 (the default), not the typed 0. `dose: parseFloat(dose) || type.default_dose` treats parseFloat('0')===0 as falsy and silently substitutes the default.
evidence: script console output: rows=[5] loggedZero=false loggedDefault=true
why: Re-ran r1-05-06: a typed 0 logs the default dose (rows=[5]) via `parseFloat(dose) || type.default_dose` (Supplements.jsx:270). But a supplement log records that he took it, so a 0 dose has no real meaning. The field is optional, placeholder-prefilled with the default (:375), and blank intentionally means the default. A typed 0 is a typo, and falling back to the default is a safe result, not nonsense output. Nothing is lost or misrecorded in a way that matters.

title: MorningCheckin (readiness/soreness/weigh-in) is completely unreachable when a workout is in-progress and today has no engine prescription — no alternate route exists
steps: With any workout_sessions row in status=in_progress and no prescription for today, open /today and look for the check-in form.
expected: The daily check-in (Energy/Mood/Soreness/weigh-in) is reachable somehow, even if a workout is mid-flight.
actual: Today.jsx:500 (`!(activeSession && !prescription)`) suppresses PrescribedSessionCard entirely in this state, and PrescribedSessionCard is the ONLY place MorningCheckin is imported/rendered anywhere in the app (confirmed by grep across src/). The intended r1-08 test (verify readiness/soreness commit even when the weight write is forced to fail) could not be run through the real UI because the form never renders at all — this is a more fundamental gap than the one the case set out to probe. Two in-progress workout_sessions rows currently exist on the shared test account (one tagged OVN-r1-03 Lift, a leftover from an earlier round; one untagged, real-looking data) — neither was touched, per ground rules, since deleting either would be altering state not created by this test.
evidence: script console output (controls() dump shows no Check In button reachable); Today.jsx:409-424,493-522
why: Real-user path: the subjective check-in is deliberately a pre-session gate, not an inline card. PrescribedSessionCard's Begin Session opens the 'Quick check-in first' sheet (PrescribedSessionCard.jsx:152-180, the only MorningCheckin render), and Today.jsx:517-519 documents this. So a workout in progress means he already passed or skipped the gate, and not showing it mid-workout is by design. The suppression at Today.jsx:500 also only fires when there is no training_prescription row for today, which should be rare on Nolan's account, since the Daily Engine is expected to write one daily (not verified against REST days) and common on the test account. Residual real gap: Today.jsx:500 keys on `activeSession`, not `activeSession.isFresh` (useActiveWorkoutSession.js:52; App.jsx:165 uses isFresh). An abandoned in_progress session days old, a known pattern (the stranded sessions in AUDIT_2026-07-30), therefore hides the whole block including WeighInPrompt on any no-prescription day, indefinitely. Weigh-in is still reachable via Fuel > Body, so this is a proposal, not a broken flow.
fixHint: src/pages/Today.jsx:500 - change the condition to `!(activeSession?.isFresh && !prescription)` so only a live (<12h) session suppresses the card and WeighInPrompt; a stale abandoned one no longer hides them.

title: analyze-physique edge function call fails CORS preflight — physique photo analysis is completely broken, and the failed upload orphans a storage object
steps: Open /physique, select a pose, upload a photo, tap Analyze.
expected: Photo is analyzed and a physique_entries row is created with the bodyfat estimate. (This case's actual target — whether a second same-day photo silently shifts the session-averaged BF% — requires this to work at all.)
actual: Analyze fails every time (2/2 consecutive attempts): pageerror "...functions/v1/analyze-physique due to access control checks.", console "Request header field apikey is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers." The storage upload (which runs BEFORE the analyze call in confirmUpload) still succeeds each time, leaving an orphaned object in the 'physique' bucket with no corresponding DB row and nothing shown in the UI. This blocked testing the session-averaging question entirely. Orphaned storage objects from both attempts were manually cleaned up.
evidence: script console output, 2 runs both failing identically
suspectFile: src/pages/PhysiqueTracker.jsx:39-58 (invokeAnalyzePhysique), :213-232 (confirmUpload — storage upload has no compensating cleanup on analyze failure); likely root cause is a CORS header allowlist gap on the analyze-physique Supabase Edge Function itself, not client code.
why: Real prod bug in the edge function's CORS headers. It is not a localhost/origin issue. supabase/functions/analyze-physique/index.ts:43 answers the preflight with Access-Control-Allow-Headers 'authorization, content-type', while supabase-js 2.98 (package-lock) sends `apikey` (fetchWithAuth) and `x-client-info` (DEFAULT_HEADERS) on every functions.invoke. Allow-Origin is '*', so the origin never matters. Verified live without running an analysis: a curl OPTIONS against the deployed function (v13, deployed 2026-07-19) returns exactly those headers, and a Playwright fetch from https://example.com, a non-localhost origin like GitHub Pages, fails preflight in both WebKit ('Request header field apikey is not allowed') and Chromium ('x-client-info is not allowed'). The same fetch to replan-day, whose allowlist includes apikey and x-client-info, passes. Function logs for the last 24h show only OPTIONS requests for analyze-physique and no POST ever reached it. The same narrow allowlist is in estimate-meal:21, read-nutrition-label:18, estimate-food-macros:20 and analyze-form:97 and all four deployed functions return that narrow list on a curl OPTIONS. All four are called through supabase.functions.invoke (FoodTracker.jsx:883, :944, :1017; Coach.jsx:93), so they send apikey and x-client-info too. AI food/meal estimate, the nutrition-label reader and Coach form critique are therefore broken in prod the same way (this affects the fuel and today areas). Unexplained: the header line hasn't changed since the function was created, yet physique entries exist (test account last 2026-06-15; usage.json shows 21 real ones in 90d). Nolan should check the date of his newest physique entry to see when this broke. The orphaned storage object is secondary and by design: the upload uses a stable path with upsert:true so a retry reuses it (PhysiqueTracker.jsx:219-223). The UI does show the error text (catch at :261-263). I did not run a real analysis.
fixHint: supabase/functions/analyze-physique/index.ts:43 - set Access-Control-Allow-Headers to 'authorization, x-client-info, apikey, content-type' (same in estimate-meal:21, read-nutrition-label:18, estimate-food-macros:20, analyze-form:97), then `supabase functions deploy` each one. The deploy is a prod action for Nolan, not the fixer.

title: No in-app way to delete a physique entry (confirmed at runtime)
steps: Open /physique, tap the edit (pencil/"Fix pose") icon on any entry, inspect the dialog; also inspect the entry card and full page for any delete affordance.
expected: Either a delete path exists, or the gap is confirmed and logged.
actual: Edit dialog offers pose selection only, no delete option. No delete/remove/trash affordance found anywhere on the page. Matches static analysis: updatePoseMutation is the only entry mutation in PhysiqueTracker.jsx. Verified read-only (dialog closed via Cancel, no changes submitted).
why: Confirmed read-only: updatePoseMutation (PhysiqueTracker.jsx:90) is the only entry mutation, and the Fix-pose sheet (:799-810) offers pose buttons only. This is a missing feature, but it traps bad data. scripts/compute_athlete_state.py:1450-1453 reads the newest 60 physique_entries bodyfat_estimates into compute_physique_bf_frac (:541), a session-average EWMA across all of them (the 45-day limit only returns None when the newest session is stale) that feeds the TDEE Forbes term (:1470, :1734). A bad shot (clothed, blurry, wrong lighting reading 30% BF) then skews the headline BF and keeps influencing the engine's energy estimate indefinitely, and in the app he can neither delete it nor correct its value.
fixHint: src/pages/PhysiqueTracker.jsx:90 - add a deleteEntryMutation (supabase.from('physique_entries').delete().eq('id',id).eq('created_by',user.id), then storage.from('physique').remove([photo_path]), invalidate ['physique-entries']) and a ConfirmDialog-guarded 'Delete photo' button in the Fix pose sheet at :799-810.
